The Envelope

The hierarchy page ended on an open rung. The soliton's carrier is four cells long and its envelope is tens to hundreds; those scales separate cleanly, which is exactly the condition for dropping the carrier and evolving the envelope on its own. This page builds that rung, and the question it has to answer is the project's usual one: is the reduced model the medium's own, or a fit?

It is the medium's own. The envelope obeys a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with two coefficients. One is the curvature of the band the soliton lane already gated, ω = sin(q/2). The other is the nonlinear frequency shift, and it comes in two parts that have to be measured separately: what a plane wave on a ring shows, and what a ring cannot show — the contraction a moving packet drags along with it, which softens the shift by two thirds. Put together, with nothing adjusted, they predict the soliton family's amplitude × width at — degree-cells. The exact chain, asked directly which amplitude neither grows nor decays, answers —.

The reduced model then runs the soliton lane's scene on a grid of one point per two cells at ten times the time step, reproduces the chain's envelope, and costs a thousandth as much. It also does two things the hierarchy page asked of it: it says precisely where it stops being valid, and — unexpectedly — it corrects a number the soliton page published.

Where the numbers come from

P is dispersion: half the band's curvature at the carrier. The band is sin(q/2) in closed form, so P = −sin(q₀/2)/8, and the row that checks it against the chain's own linear blocks agrees to seven digits.

Q is how much faster a wave runs when it is tall. Put a uniform wave of amplitude a on a ring and its frequency rises by Qringa², the same per a² at one degree and at two. That number holds the on-site quartic, the fold's configuration-dependent inertia, the inter-plane terms, and the strain the wave drives at its second harmonic. Across four carriers it is (1 + 4sin²(q/2))/(12 sin³(q/2)) to four digits — a closed form matched to the measurement, not derived from the energy.

But a ring of fixed length cannot contract, and a packet in an open medium does. The fold-to-strain coupling is a gradient coupling — V₃ = (STEP/2) Σ γ²ₙ(un+1 − un−1), measured term by term — so a moving packet drives the strain chain with the gradient of its own |A|² and drags a dent along with it, a contraction of depth −STEP⟨γ²⟩/(2 − 8vg²). Sitting in its own dent the packet is softer, and the frequency shift drops by Qdent = −STEP²/(16ω₀(2 − 8vg²)), which is exactly −1/(6 sin³(q/2)). At the soliton's carrier the ring gives — and the dent takes back —. A derivation that forgot the dent would be off by a factor of three in Q, and would predict a soliton family half the size.

The page integrates the equation in the header — split-step Fourier, 256 points across a ring of 360 cells, time step 0.5 — every time it loads, and draws its envelope against the exact chain's envelope from the gated Python model, frame for frame. The chain took twenty thousand steps of a 720-coordinate system to make its side of the picture; the envelope model makes its side in a few milliseconds.

The badge is the page's honesty. It reports the largest gap between the envelope model's |A| and the chain's envelope over the whole run, as a fraction of the peak, and then re-runs the model with Q deliberately 30% wrong and reports that too, so that a reader can see the check is able to fail. The gap that remains with the right Q is the chain's own breathing about the exact lattice soliton — a width-8 packet is only two carrier wavelengths across, and the envelope model has no lattice to breathe against.

the collision · warm and cold · a published number corrected

What the collision actually shifts

Two envelopes travelling opposite ways couple through cross-phase modulation alone: each sees the other's |B|² with a coefficient Qx, measured the same way Q was — two waves on a ring, plus the dent the other packet carries. Run the coupled envelope model's head-on collision and each soliton comes out displaced by — cells. The soliton page measured 0.63 in the chain. The envelope model is not wrong; the 0.63 was mostly not the collision.

A packet launched cold — with the strain at rest, as the soliton page launched it — radiates a pulse of strain while its dent forms. The pulse travels at c = ½, faster than the packet at vg = 0.354, so it runs ahead, crosses the ring, and passes through the other packet, which is shifted by it. Two packets launched cold each receive the other's pulse; a single packet launched cold receives only its own; and the difference between the two runs was read as the collision. Launch the same two packets warm — with the dent each would have dragged had it been travelling forever already in place — and the chain's shift is — cells, which is the envelope model's number. The cold launch reproduces the old one, —.

Every number in the soliton page's collision row stands as measured. What changes is what it measured: a strain pulse from the launch, with a small true collision shift underneath it. The collision is still nearly elastic, both packets still come out at full height, and it is still something a linear medium cannot do — but its signature is a tenth of a cell, and rung 4 predicts it.

Where rung 4 stops

Below, the lattice. The envelope model has no cells. At width 2 it holds its own family member's height where the chain loses a fifth of it; that is the discreteness wall from the soliton lane, seen from the side that cannot see it.

Toward long carriers, the strain. The dent grows like 1/sin³(q/2) and takes 2w/(c − vg) to form, a time that diverges as the group velocity approaches the sound speed. The adiabatic Q, ring plus dent, is (1 − 2cos q)/(12 sin³(q/2)): it vanishes at carrier π/3 — the ring's 4/3 against the dent's −4/3, measured — and turns defocusing below it. Yet at carrier π/4 the chain packet focuses, hard, for hundreds of time units: its dent is only half formed by t = 600, and until it forms the packet runs on the bare ring coefficient. The single-envelope equation assumes its long-wave fields keep up with it instantly, and that assumption is exactly what fails at the resonance. Beyond it the strain is a slow field of its own, coupled to the envelope, not a coefficient inside it — a different and larger equation, which this page does not build.

Scope. Everything is at the soliton lane's carrier, q₀ = π/2, except where a row says otherwise; the plane-symmetric restriction is inherited from the chain, and the chain's own gate against the seven-coordinate medium is what makes this page a reduction of the model of record rather than of a model of it. The closed forms for the ring shift and for Q are matched to measurement at four carriers, not derived from the energy. The mean fold — the breathe, which is gapless — is not driven by a plane wave at this order (the fold's inertia gradient is exactly −4·STEP, and the two sources cancel), but near the resonance the chain shows it pumped to degrees; it belongs to the larger equation beyond the wall. The lanes this builds on: The Wave That Holds, Two Fields, A Million Cells.
